data.title: Oracle (ORCL) Adds Federal Veterans And Military Care To Its Health Data Network
data.description:

In fact, the recent purchase by Alexander Toeldte was the biggest purchase of Clearwater Paper shares made by an insider individual in the last twelve months, according to our records. That implies that an insider found the current price of US$16.76 per share to be enticing. That means they have been optimistic about the company in the past, though they may have changed their mind. Looking at the total insider shareholdings in a company can help to inform your view of whether they are well aligned with common shareholders. Usually, the higher the insider ownership, the more likely it is that insiders will be incentivised to build the company for the long term. data.title: The Bet Behind Hitachi Energy India's Rally
data.description:
If you only skimmed the headlines, the MoU that tied Hitachi Energy India into CATL’s next generation TENER+ grid storage roll out in Australia looked like just another partnership announcement. For Hitachi Energy India shareholders, the return from the start of the year was 68.4%, including dividends. If you had been deciding on 1 January 2026, what would you have needed to believe about future grid projects and earnings quality for that outcome to feel realistic?

This theme extends beyond Hitachi Energy India. See which of 41 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks may still merit a closer look.

The Two Hitachi Energy India Stories Investors Were Weighing

The shares cost ₹18,482 at the start of the period, and the real question was which story about Hitachi Energy India felt more plausible to you.

The bullish view implied a Fair Value of ₹20,557, effectively the price suggested if assumptions played out. It was built on a record ₹29,135 crore order backlog and expectations for 39.0% annual revenue growth with profit margins reaching 11.3% over three years.

The bearish story pointed to a Fair Value of ₹13,350, based on concerns that dependence on long public sector and HVDC contracts, plus global supply chains, could keep cash flow and net margins under pressure.

What The Evidence Did To The Hitachi Energy India Argument

The MoU tying Hitachi Energy India into CATL’s TENER+ rollout in Australia supported the bullish story about export orders and complex grid projects. The Q2 2027 report showed revenue at ₹29,965.1m and net income at ₹3,184.9m compared with ₹18,325.5m and ₹2,643.6m, while net margin moved from 14.4% to 10.6%. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The key assumption investors needed to watch was earnings quality. When assessing another grid supplier, track whether net margin trends keep pace with revenue and profit headlines instead of relying only on backlog or new partnerships.

What Hitachi Energy India’s Run Leaves You Paying For Now

With Hitachi Energy India at ₹31,120, this Narrative’s Fair Value is described as sitting above the current price, according to the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St, rather than as a settled fact.

data.title: 3 ETFs For Owning Moderna After Its Melanoma Trial Whipsaw
data.description:
You can own Moderna directly and carry the company’s full ride in your account, or you can hold it through a fund that owns many businesses at once. Simply Wall St flags recent heavy insider selling and a very jumpy share price over the last three months. An exchange traded fund that includes Moderna spreads how much those swings affect your portfolio, and also spreads out any gains from the stock.

Moderna just saw its shares spike after positive test results for a melanoma vaccine used with a cancer drug, followed by a pullback as investors weighed future costs and questions on how broadly the treatment might work. That kind of mixed but important news is why some investors look at iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB), VanEck Biotech ETF (BBH), or iShares Genomics Immunology and Healthcare ETF (IDNA) as ways to own Moderna inside a wider mix of healthcare stocks.

Rather choose individual stocks than a fund? Explore 37 high quality undervalued stocks.

iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB)

Gilead Sciences and Amgen anchor the top of IBB, alongside other biotechnology stocks such as Vertex Pharmaceuticals. You get most of your exposure in this ETF to biotechnology at 88.2% of the portfolio, with extra coverage in life sciences tools and services and a smaller slice in pharmaceuticals. Within that mix, Moderna is a meaningful position. It ranks fifth in the fund at 5.67% of assets, so roughly US$57 of every US$1,000 in IBB tracks Moderna rather than the wider biotech group.

Simply Wall St highlights significant insider selling at Moderna over the past three months, which can worry some investors when they own the single stock. IBB cannot blunt that specific concern, since Gilead Sciences, Amgen and many other holdings operate in the same broad sector and face their own management decisions. What you do gain with IBB is exposure to hundreds of biotechnology and related healthcare businesses instead of tying everything to Moderna alone.

Not every stock inside IBB is priced the same way. Find out how many of IBB's holdings look undervalued.

VanEck Biotech ETF (BBH)

BBH gives Moderna a real slice of your biotech allocation at 7% of the portfolio, so US$70 of every US$1,000 tracks the stock. The rest of the ETF looks a lot like IBB, with heavy exposure to biotechnology alongside life sciences tools and services. Amgen is much larger here at 16.8%, and Gilead Sciences also has a double digit weight, so your money leans toward a tight group of big biotech stocks rather than a very broad spread.

Moderna has had a volatile share price over the past three months compared to the US market, and BBH only partly softens that because over 80% of assets sit in the same biotechnology industry and can move together. This means the fund spreads your risk across several large drug developers but leaves the sector’s ups and downs largely intact.

Uncover whether BBH has kept pace with the market over the past week, year and five years

iShares Genomics Immunology and Healthcare ETF (IDNA)

IDNA tilts heavily toward biotechnology at 68.3% of assets, with another 27.2% in pharmaceuticals and a smaller slice in life sciences tools and services. Moderna sits right at the top of that mix, with about US$140 of every US$1,000 in the fund tied to the stock, so it is a real part of what you would own. The balance comes from other healthcare specialists such as Genmab and Twist Bioscience, which pull more of your money into different approaches to genomics and immunology than Moderna alone.

One question with Moderna is how reliably its products can support the business over time. IDNA spreads that risk across companies whose revenue leans on other treatment areas and markets, which can help if Moderna hits a rough patch. A large chunk of the ETF still depends on a narrow group of high science healthcare stocks, so you are ultimately counting on that whole corner of the market to keep delivering.

Ten companies make up 51.6% of IDNA. Find out which ones, and how much each carries.

Choosing how much Moderna you really want

The choice across IBB, BBH and IDNA comes down to how tightly you want to link your money to Moderna after that headline grabbing melanoma trial jump and pullback. IDNA is the most concentrated on the stock, with about US$140 of every US$1,000 going into Moderna, and the highest fee at roughly US$47 a year on a US$10,000 holding. BBH lands in the middle. You pay about US$35 a year in fees and get around US$70 in Moderna for every US$1,000, inside a 27 stock biotech heavy fund.

IBB spreads your risk widest, with 248 holdings and roughly US$57 of every US$1,000 tied to Moderna, although the fund still leans on biotech and related healthcare businesses. That breadth can matter if Moderna’s share price swings sharply again, given Simply Wall St flags recent volatility against the US market. Your decision is simple. If you want the strongest focus on Moderna you look closer to IDNA. If you prefer more companies around it for the same dollar, IBB sits at the other end, with BBH as a concentrated middle ground.

With 16.8% of BBH riding on Amgen, its next few years matter as much as the fund's. See the earnings forecasts for Amgen.

data.title: Have Insiders Sold Corpay Shares Recently?
data.description:
We wouldn't blame Corpay, Inc. (NYSE:CPAY) shareholders if they were a little worried about the fact that Ronald Clarke, the Chairman recently netted about US$85m selling shares at an average price of US$441. However, it's crucial to note that they remain very much invested in the stock and that sale only reduced their holding by 8.2%.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Corpay

Notably, that recent sale by Ronald Clarke is the biggest insider sale of Corpay shares that we've seen in the last year. So it's clear an insider wanted to take some cash off the table, even below the current price of US$454. We generally consider it a negative if insiders have been selling, especially if they did so below the current price, because it implies that they considered a lower price to be reasonable. However, while insider selling is sometimes discouraging, it's only a weak signal. This single sale was just 8.2% of Ronald Clarke's stake.

In total, Corpay insiders sold more than they bought over the last year. The chart below shows insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year. If you want to know exactly who sold, for how much, and when, simply click on the graph below!

See our latest analysis for Corpay

For those who like to find hidden gems this free list of small cap companies with recent insider purchasing, could be just the ticket.

Does Corpay Boast High Insider Ownership?

For a common shareholder, it is worth checking how many shares are held by company insiders. Usually, the higher the insider ownership, the more likely it is that insiders will be incentivised to build the company for the long term. Corpay insiders own about US$1.0b worth of shares (which is 3.6% of the company). Most shareholders would be happy to see this sort of insider ownership, since it suggests that management incentives are well aligned with other shareholders.

So What Do The Corpay Insider Transactions Indicate?

An insider sold stock recently, but they haven't been buying. And our longer term analysis of insider transactions didn't bring confidence, either. But it is good to see that Corpay is growing earnings. It is good to see high insider ownership, but the insider selling leaves us cautious. While it's good to be aware of what's going on with the insider's ownership and transactions, we make sure to also consider what risks are facing a stock before making any investment decision. Case in point: We've spotted 2 warning signs for Corpay you should be aware of, and 1 of them is concerning.

Of course, you might find a fantastic investment by looking elsewhere. So take a peek at this free list of interesting companies.

For the purposes of this article, insiders are those individuals who report their transactions to the relevant regulatory body. We currently account for open market transactions and private dispositions of direct interests only, but not derivative transactions or indirect interests.
